effectiveness.claim: The record does not verify prevention or effective correction of the named inspection/safety failures. Detection and vendor change are not a completed remedy.

evidence.claim: ICE policy required a Custody Management Division pre-occupancy inspection; the contract incorporated detention standards.
evidence.limits: Underlying policy/contract not independently reread here; this is the retained GAO audit account.

period.note: Policy date reported by GAO; the obligation applied to the 2025 opening.

evidence.claim: Occupancy began August 16 without the required pre-occupancy inspection. GAO found no effective control preventing occupancy before inspection and standards compliance.
evidence.limits: Specific opening-gate failure; not proof that every inspection or later safeguard failed.

period.note: Dates describe the retained record, not a new observation.

evidence.claim: ICE oversight operated after occupancy: the February 2026 ODO inspection rated the facility acceptable while identifying 49 deficiencies, including three priority issues.
evidence.limits: Inspection/detection is observed operation. A rating does not show that any named deficiency was corrected.

period.note: Dates describe the retained record, not a new observation.

evidence.claim: September GAO observations included inadequate recreation, missing accessible showers and understaffed camera monitoring; the December discrepancy report documented substituted TB questionnaires and a November TB case in general population.
evidence.limits: Table 1 does not evaluate post-September fixes; report dates are not automatically dates of every underlying event.

period.note: Dates describe the retained record, not a new observation.

evidence.claim: A recreation yard opened but remained inadequate on September 16; a replacement contract was awarded March 12 and the first contract terminated in April.
evidence.limits: Concrete activity/partial improvement, not demonstrated correction of the inspection gate or medical/safety failures. GAO could not yet assess replacement effectiveness.

period.note: Dates describe the retained record, not a new observation.

evidence.claim: DHS asserted existing inspection policy was adequate and requested closure; GAO rejected that sufficiency because policy had not prevented uninspected occupancy.
evidence.limits: Preserves agency position and GAO disagreement; the response is not an implementation or outcome record.

period.note: Dates describe the retained record, not a new observation.

evidence.claim: Defense agreed to a lessons assessment while disputing GAO conclusions and balance; GAO maintained that both agencies made consequential decisions.
evidence.limits: Underlying rebuttal was not independently read; disagreement does not by itself resolve the factual inspection failure.

period.note: Dates describe the retained record, not a new observation.

evidence.claim: The October 12 retained GAO product-page recheck marks the inspection-control recommendation Open and preserves DHS’s reliance on existing policy and GAO’s disagreement.
evidence.limits: Paraphrased page observation, not a new HTTP capture or independent source. Open is not proof that no corrective work occurred; closure would not be a full safety certification.

period.note: Dates describe the retained record, not a new observation.

failure.claim: The inspection gate failed at the August 16, 2025 opening; additional dated noncompliance is documented. Later operation does not erase this historical finding.

formal.claim: Pre-occupancy inspection and detention-standard requirements existed.

output.function: Keep each safeguard claim within its cited evidence class and scope.

authority.claim: ICE had oversight responsibilities and exercised inspection functions, but GAO found no effective occupancy-prevention control. Usable stop authority was not demonstrated at opening.

people.claim: Inspectors and oversight personnel demonstrably acted after occupancy; pre-opening staffing/readiness was not established.

procedures.claim: Later inspections and discrepancy reporting operated, while the required opening procedure was skipped.

output.task: The pre-occupancy inspection gate at the August 2025 opening and later evidence of inspection activity and remedy at Camp East Montana; later activity cannot repair the historical fact of uninspected opening.

comparisons.explanation: Officials cited an expedited opening timeline for the omission. That explains the reported administrative choice without satisfying the required inspection.

contrary_evidence.claim: Real later inspections, discrepancy reports, a partial recreation improvement and a contractor change contradict a blanket assertion that nothing was done. They do not establish effective correction.
DHS sought closure based on existing policy, and Defense disputed the audit framing; both responses are retained with GAO’s disagreement.
Open recommendation status tracks GAO follow-up, not the absence of all corrective activity. It neither erases observed steps nor verifies an effective occupancy gate.

next_test.required_record: The same one-record TB follow-up proposed in the preserved Camp case; public official findings tied to the named requirements.
next_test.stop_condition: Stop after one qualifying public record or an explicit unavailable/access-limited outcome; do not infer either side from silence.
next_test.supports_if: It records completed testing/notification changes and verifies that they satisfied the requirements in the inspected scope.
next_test.weakens_if: It records persistent deficiencies, incomplete fixes or only promises/overall ratings; absence of a record leaves correction unknown.

output.summary: A later inspection cannot retroactively satisfy a pre-occupancy gate. Effective medical/safety correction after transition remains unverified. Preserve the existing case’s one bounded TB follow-up rather than creating another collection queue. Pricing nonimplementation documented elsewhere as of August is a separate outcome, not proof of inspection or medical correction. The retained October 12 status observation adds no item-level medical or safety closure record; effectiveness remains unknown and the historical opening failure remains documented.
The record does not verify prevention or effective correction of the named inspection/safety failures. Detection and vendor change are not a completed remedy.
